title: Fit a Linear Regression Model in scikit-learn
prompt: Using LinearRegression from sklearn.linear_model, fit a model on X = np.array([[10], [20], [30], [40]]) and y = np.array([25, 45, 65, 85]), then store the prediction for [[50]] as float in pred_50.
solution:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

X = np.array([[10], [20], [30], [40]])
y = np.array([25, 45, 65, 85])
model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
pred_50 = float(model.predict([[50]])[0])
explanation: y = 2*x + 5, so predicting at x=50 gives 105.0.

title: What is overfitting?
hints: High train score, low test score
solution: When a model memorizes training data noise and generalizes poorly to unseen test data.
front: What is overfitting in machine learning?
back: When a model fits training data (and its noise) too closely, performing well on training data but poorly on unseen test data.

title: Data leakage prevention
solution: Split into train and test BEFORE fitting scalers, encoders, or models.
front: Why must you run `train_test_split` before fitting a scaler or imputer?
back: To prevent **data leakage**: computing means or min/max across the whole dataset leaks test-set information into training.
